Ajaccio cruise port is located on the western coast of Corsica. The port city is the largest on the island and is famous with the fact that it is the birthplace of Napoleon. Ajaccio cruise port is situated in the Gulf of Ajaccio.  The city covers a total area of approx 82 km2 (31,67 ml2) and has a population of around 68,600 people (2014 census). It attracts tourist with its unusual shops and amazing restaurants. Ajaccio is easily explored only on foot and has one of the most breathtaking harbours in the world. The city is French but still there is some Italian influence.

  • The port of Ajaccio is linked with mainland France on an almost daily basis (Toulon, Nice, Marseille). There are also occasional connections to mainland Italy (Livorno) and to Sardinia, along with a seasonal service serving Propriano and Calvi. The major shipping companies providing the links are Corsica Ferries and SNCM.
  • Ajaccio has become a stopover for cruise vacations with a total of more than 418,000 passengers (2007), the largest in Corsica and the 2nd-largest in France (following Marseille, but ahead of Nice and Cannes). Ajaccio aims for eventually becoming the premier French port for cruises and a main departure point. The city's port function is also served by commercial, pleasure craft, artisanal fisheries (three ports).
  • Ajaccio cruise port is in the itineraries of major cruise lines including Costa Cruises, Royal Caribbean International, AIDA, Princess Cruises, Oceania Cruises, Regent, Silversea, MSC Cruises, Pullmantur Cruises, Holland America Line, Cunard, Seabourn and Phoenix.

Ajaccio cruise terminal

Ajaccio cruise port is a tender port. Cruise ships anchor in the harbour and their passengers are transported via the ship's tender boats to the pier. The cruise terminal is located at Quai L’Herminier. On its east side is the ferry terminal and on the west side is the fishing port. Ajaccio cruise port terminal is small but modern and is known as Gare Maritime.

The terminal offers booking desks, telephones, toilets and taxi services. Ajaccio International Airport is 7 km from Ajaccio cruise port terminal. The city highlights are within walking distance. You have to head left outside the terminal and continue along the road for half a kilometre to reach the heart of the city.

If you want to use a taxi, be aware to negotiate the price. There is a taxi rank near Ajaccio cruise port terminal. The official language of the area is French, the currency – Euro.

At a Glance

Independent sightseeing: Easy independently. Ajaccio is one of Corsica's simplest cruise calls to explore without an organized tour. The historic center, Napoleon-related sights, market, waterfront and Saint-François Beach are all close to the port. Transport is mainly needed for the Pointe de la Parata, the Sanguinaires coastline or excursions into the Corsican countryside.

Ajaccio should not be considered a tender-only port. The commercial port has a dedicated cruise berth at the Môle Croisières, while Quai l'Herminier is also equipped for cruise tenders. Whether a particular ship docks or anchors can therefore depend on ship size, berth allocation and other traffic. Passengers arriving by tender are normally landed in the same central port area.

Getting from the Cruise Port

The passenger exit is beside the Gare Maritime and Quai l'Herminier, directly on the edge of central Ajaccio. Place Foch and the entrance to the old town are roughly 0.3-0.5 km (0.2-0.3 mi) away, normally a 5-10 minute walk along the waterfront. A shuttle is not normally necessary for city sightseeing.

  • Walking: Best for the old town, Maison Bonaparte, cathedral, Palais Fesch, market and nearby beach.
  • Bus: Muvistrada Line 5 links the central Place de Gaulle area with the Route des Sanguinaires and Pointe de la Parata. Check the current timetable before setting out.
  • Taxi: Useful for La Parata, beaches farther along the Sanguinaires road or a private countryside trip.
  • Train: Ajaccio railway station is about 0.6 km (0.4 mi) from the Gare Maritime, but rail trips inland are generally less convenient than local sightseeing during a normal cruise call.

Best Ways to Spend Your Time

Old Town and Napoleon Sites

Allow 2.5-4 hours. Easy independently. This is the most practical choice for a first visit. Walk from the port through central Ajaccio to Place Foch, the narrow streets of the old Genoese quarter, Maison Bonaparte and the Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta. Maison Bonaparte, Napoleon's birthplace, normally takes about 45 minutes to visit.

Art visitors can add the Palais Fesch, whose collection usually needs another 1-1.5 hours. If your ship arrives in the morning, the Marcatu d'Aiacciu at Place Campinchi is also an easy stop; the main market operates in the morning from Tuesday to Sunday. The Citadelle Miollis is undergoing a major rehabilitation, so public access can change and it is safest to treat it primarily as an exterior sightseeing stop unless access is confirmed on the day.

Pointe de la Parata and the Sanguinaires Islands View

Allow about 3-4 hours including transport. Independent with some planning or transport. Pointe de la Parata lies about 11 km (6.8 mi) west of central Ajaccio at the end of the scenic Route des Sanguinaires. It is one of the best options if you want coastal scenery rather than museums.

Muvistrada Line 5 runs from Place de Gaulle toward La Parata; a taxi is faster and easier when time ashore is limited. At the Grand Site, allow about 45 minutes for the signed walk toward the Genoese tower and viewpoints over the Sanguinaires Islands. The final approach to the tower includes fairly steep steps. Bus passengers should check the return timetable before starting the walk, as missing a service can significantly reduce the return margin.

Saint-François or Trottel Beach

Allow 2-4 hours. Easy independently. Saint-François is the easiest beach for cruise passengers, around 0.7 km (0.4 mi) from the port area beside the historic center and citadel. It works well as a swimming stop after a walking tour.

Trottel Beach is farther west along the waterfront and is larger, with restaurants nearby. It can be reached on foot from central Ajaccio or by Muvistrada Lines 2 or 5. Both beaches have seasonal lifeguard coverage during July and August, but swimming conditions and supervision should always be checked locally.

Prunelli Valley and Lake Tolla

Allow roughly 4-6 hours. Organized excursion or pre-arranged transport recommended. Passengers wanting mountain scenery can head inland through the Prunelli Valley toward villages, forested gorges and Lake Tolla. The lake is about 30 km (18.6 mi) from Ajaccio and roughly 30 minutes away by road under normal conditions.

This is much less convenient by public transport than central Ajaccio or La Parata. A ship excursion, private driver or carefully planned rental car is preferable, particularly because the mountain roads are slower than the distance may suggest and road delays can reduce the return margin.

Self-Guided Walking Tour

Old Ajaccio, Napoleon and the Waterfront

Distance: approximately 3 km (1.9 mi). Pure walking time: about 40-45 minutes. Recommended total time: 2.5-4 hours with sightseeing stops. Difficulty: Easy. The route is mostly level, although the old town has narrow streets, paving stones and occasional uneven surfaces.

  1. Gare Maritime / cruise passenger exit: Leave the port and follow the waterfront toward central Ajaccio.
  2. Palais Fesch: See the museum and Imperial Chapel complex. Enter the museum only if you can spare about 1-1.5 hours.
  3. Place Campinchi and the market: A useful morning stop for Corsican cheese, charcuterie, produce and local specialties. The market is closed on Mondays.
  4. Place Foch: Continue into the historic center and the compact Genoese old town.
  5. Maison Bonaparte: Visit Napoleon's birthplace or simply see its exterior if time is short.
  6. Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta: A few minutes from Maison Bonaparte and closely associated with Napoleon's early life.
  7. Citadelle Miollis and Saint-François Beach: Walk along the waterfront side of the old quarter for views of the citadel and, in warm weather, an optional beach stop. Citadel access can be restricted during the current redevelopment.
  8. Place de Gaulle and waterfront return: Finish at the broad seafront square, then walk back toward the Gare Maritime.

If visiting the market, do that section early in the day. Adding both Maison Bonaparte and the full Palais Fesch visit can turn the route into a 4-hour outing; with exterior stops only, it can comfortably be completed in around 1.5-2 hours.

Practical Tips

  • Check the ship's daily program to confirm whether your call is alongside or by tender. Tendering requires additional time both going ashore and returning.
  • Central Ajaccio is compact enough that there is little benefit in taking transport between the principal historic sights.
  • For La Parata, confirm the current Line 5 timetable before leaving the center and allow for summer traffic along the Route des Sanguinaires.
  • Museum opening days and hours vary by season, so check them before building the day around an indoor visit.
  • For a docked ship, aim to return to the port area with a generous margin before all-aboard. Allow still more time when tendering or returning from La Parata or the countryside.
